**NovaBio Therapeutics - Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript**

**Operator:**  
Good morning, and welcome to the NovaBio Therapeutics Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question during this time, please press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.  

I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Johnson, Vice President of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

**Sarah Johnson, Vice President of Investor Relations:**  
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss NovaBio Therapeutics' financial results for the third quarter of 2024. Joining me on today's call are Dr. Emily Carter, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Reynolds, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Lisa Patel, Chief Medical Officer; and Dr. Raj Singh, Chief Scientific Officer.  

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's call will contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.  

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Emily Carter, CEO of NovaBio Therapeutics.

**Dr. Emily Carter, CEO:**  
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. NovaBio Therapeutics delivered a strong performance in the third quarter, driven by robust product sales growth, key regulatory milestones, and continued pipeline advancement. We continue to make significant progress on our key strategic priorities, including expanding our oncology and rare disease franchises, scaling new indications for market-leading therapies, and investing efficiently in high-potential R&D programs.  

Our regulatory achievements this quarter were transformative, with full FDA approvals and label expansions that significantly broaden our addressable markets. In oncology, we're seeing tremendous traction with our immuno-oncology assets, while in rare diseases, gene therapy expansions are driving royalty growth. We've also made solid headway on new product launches and early market share gains in competitive spaces like GLP-1s and ADCs. These efforts are complemented by disciplined operating expense management and a fortified balance sheet that supports ongoing innovation.  

We are particularly excited about NovaKine-7 and its potential to redefine frontline NSCLC treatment, with label expansions unlocking billions in peak sales.  

Now, I will turn the call over to Michael Reynolds, our CFO, to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

**Michael Reynolds, CFO:**  
Thank you, Emily. As Emily mentioned, we had a solid third quarter. Revenue for the quarter was $3.95 billion, an increase of 28% compared to the same period last year. This increase was primarily driven by higher net sales from NovaKine-7, which generated $285 million—a 62% year-over-year jump—alongside $410 million in royalties from BioGenix-RD1 ex-U.S. licensing to Roche, up 35%, and contributions from new launches like Zepara and OncoVance.  

Our GAAP net income for the quarter was $850 million, or $2.45 per share. Non-GAAP net income was $975 million, or $2.82 per share.  

Turning to operating expenses, which totaled $1.72 billion, up 12% year-over-year but representing 44% of revenues as we expanded adjusted non-GAAP operating margins to 28%. This discipline reflects strategic investments across our late-stage pipeline while achieving efficiencies that outpace peers. R&D was the largest component at $1.12 billion, or 65% of OpEx and up 18% YoY, driven by pipeline advancement in immuno-oncology and gene therapies—think $450 million in externalized trial costs for programs like NeoVax-PD1 in NSCLC and BNX-301 for Duchenne, offset by 15% per-patient savings from optimized sites in Eastern Europe. We also allocated $320 million to early-stage innovation via our AI platform, yielding new INDs for KRAS inhibitors, with headcount efficiencies bringing our R&D output to 1.4 times the industry average. SG&A came in at $520 million, up just 5% YoY, with $280 million in commercial scaling for assets like NeoCortix, including sales force growth and digital campaigns that boosted patient starts, alongside G&A savings from outsourcing and shared services. Other OpEx was $80 million, tied to acquisition integration. Looking ahead, we see Q4 OpEx at $1.75-1.80 billion, with portfolio pruning freeing up capital.  

R&D expense specifically hit $452 million in Q3, up 15% YoY, tracking to the high end of $1.85-1.90 billion for the year at about 28% of revenues—right in line with peers like Regeneron and Vertex. This increase stems from late-stage acceleration and manufacturing scale-up, partially offset by 22% cost reductions in early screening via AI. We externalized 65% of spend to CROs and CMOs, keeping R&D headcount flat at 1,850. Oncology took 48% or $217 million, prioritizing ADCs like PGX-ADC-301 in Phase 3 for HER2-low breast cancer, with $85 million on global enrollment. Immunology got 25% or $113 million for bispecifics like PGX-BSP-102 in Phase 3 for psoriatic arthritis, and rare diseases 20% or $90 million for AAV gene therapy PGX-GT-501. Regionally, 55% U.S., 45% ex-U.S. for cost arbitrage. Our priorities—de-risking Phase II/III assets, AI platform leverage nominating five targets, and virtual trial efficiencies—position us for $25 billion risk-adjusted NPV and 20%+ CAGR.  

Before diving deeper into financials, let's highlight our pivotal regulatory milestones this quarter, where we notched three major approvals and two label expansions across oncology and rare diseases, unlocking $4.2 billion in incremental peak sales over five years and expanding our TAM by 28% to over $12 billion globally. Leading this is full FDA approval of NovaKine-7, our PD-1/VEGF bispecific, for first-line advanced NSCLC with high PD-L1 (TPS ≥50%), building on its second-line approval where it holds 18% U.S. share. The sNDA drew from Phase 3 NOVALUNG-301 (n=1,024), showing 48.2% ORR vs. 32.1% for pembro (p<0.0001), 11.4-month mPFS vs. 7.8 (HR 0.62), and 72% 12-month OS vs. 61%, with Grade 3+ TRAEs at 22%. This doubles U.S. patients to 95,000, lifting peak sales to $2.1 billion; EMA CHMP positive last week eyes Q1 2025 approval, NMPA priority review taps China's $1.2 billion market. We're rolling a BLA for NovaKine-7 plus NovaTox-19 ADC combo in TNBC (65% ORR Phase 2). In rare diseases, full approval of AAV9 gene therapy BioGenix-RD1 for SMA Type 2 (ages 2+), with orphan and RMAT designations; Phase 3 EXPAND-2 (n=168) hit 89% standing vs. 12%, +12.4 HFMSE points, 94% event-free survival. Adds 4,200 U.S. patients, $1.8 billion peak; EMA PRIME-approved, Japan PMDA Q4 2024. Smaller wins: NovaDerm-45 biosimilar for pediatric atopic dermatitis ($450 million peak) and NovaKine-7 NMPA for HCC (35% ORR). Our 85% Phase 3 success rate beats industry's 55%, fueling 25% CAGR and FY24 revenue guide to $3.8-4.0 billion.  

On new product launches and share gains, Zepara, our GLP-1/GIP agonist, posted $285 million Q3 sales, up 170% sequentially post-Q4 2023 U.S. launch, beating guidance; IQVIA shows 14.2% NBRx share in GLP-1s, 9.8% TRx, gaining from Ozempic/Wegovy via better tolerability, with 85% payer access at $1,050 WAC. U.S. 92%, early EU €22 million, China via Sinopharm eyes $2.5 billion ex-U.S. peak. OncoVance ADC hit $112 million, 11.5% share in HER2 space vs. Kadcyla, fueled by capacity expansion; sNDA frontline pending. Combined peaks over $8 billion.  

Our cash position remains strong at $6.8 billion. Operating cash flow was $925 million, up 42% YoY, from ZyntraVex-like sales and rebates; free cash flow $715 million. Balance sheet net cash $3.9 billion, current ratio 2.8x. Year-to-date FCF $2.1 billion funds M&A.  

For the full year, we are updating our guidance to revenue of $3.8-4.0 billion, R&D $2.0-2.1 billion, with strong EPS growth.  

Now, I'll turn the call over to Dr. Lisa Patel, our Chief Medical Officer, to discuss our clinical programs.

**Dr. Lisa Patel, Chief Medical Officer:**  
Thank you, Michael. We are very pleased with the progress of our clinical trials. Specifically, programs like PGX-ADC-301 are fully enrolled in Phase 3, PGX-BSP-102 advanced post-strong Phase 2b, and PGX-GT-501 dosing pediatrics under RMAT. Regulatory wins like NovaKine-7 frontline and BioGenix-RD1 expansions de-risk further, with topline data for key trials like DESTINY-Advance in Q2 2025 and multiple BLAs ahead. We expect to report 5-7 readouts next year, advancing our $15 billion pipeline.  

Now, I'll hand the call back to Emily.

**Dr. Emily Carter, CEO:**  
Thank you, Lisa. We will now open the call for questions.

**Operator:**  
Ladies and gentlemen, at this time we will begin the question-and-answer session. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

**John Smith, Goldman Sachs:**  
Thanks, good morning. Congrats on the quarter. On the NovaKine-7 frontline approval, can you elaborate on pricing strategy and expected share trajectory versus Keytruda and Libtayo, especially with EMA and China timelines?

**Dr. Emily Carter, CEO:**  
Good morning, John. Thanks for the question. Pricing for NovaKine-7 frontline will align with our second-line at around $180,000 annual WAC, supporting premium positioning given superior PFS and OS data from NOVALUNG-301. We're targeting 20-25% U.S. share within 12 months via KOL advocacy and our 1,200-rep oncology force, directly challenging Keytruda's dominance—our cleaner safety should drive switches. EMA Q1 2025 launch leverages CHMP momentum for quick reimbursement, and Sinopharm accelerates China mid-2025 into a high-growth market. Early U.S. traction at 18% second-line bodes well.

**Operator:**  
Our next question comes from Maria Lopez with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

**Maria Lopez, JPMorgan:**  
Hi, thanks. Michael, on R&D spend acceleration to $452 million, how are you thinking about 2025 guidance amid IRA risks and ADC competition? Any updates on AI platform ROI?

**Michael Reynolds, CFO:**  
Hi Maria. Our Q3 R&D uptick reflects Phase 3 investments like $85 million on PGX-ADC-301, but efficiencies from AI—slashing discovery by 30%—keep us at 25-30% of revenues. 2025 guide will be $2.1-2.2 billion, with 70% in late-stage (>50% PoS). IRA mitigations via ex-U.S. ramp (45% spend) and premium biologics; ADC leadership mirrors Enhertu, diversified across oncology (48%), immunology (25%). AI has nominated five targets, enabling Roche deal—ROI already at 3x via faster preclinicals.

**Operator:**  
Our next question comes from David Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

**David Chen, Morgan Stanley:**  
Thanks, team. Lisa, thoughts on BioGenix-RD1 Type 2 expansion durability versus Zolgensma, and any color on upcoming gene therapy CMC hurdles for PGX-GT-501?

**Dr. Lisa Patel, Chief Medical Officer:**  
David, great question. EXPAND-2 data shows 94% event-free survival at 24 months and superior motor gains versus supportive care, with our lipid nanoparticle profile lowering immunogenicity risks compared to Zolgensma—92% Type 1 penetration already proves real-world strength. Royalties up 35% YoY. For PGX-GT-501 DMD, we're investing 15% of rare disease budget in process optimization at our Boston facility to hit $2-3 million COGS, aligning with Elevidys de-risking; RMAT fast-tracks pediatric data, with enrollment on track despite CMC challenges industry-wide.

**Operator:**  
Our next question comes from Alex Rivera with Barclays. Please go ahead.

**Alex Rivera, Barclays:**  
Morning, all. On Zepara and OncoVance launches, how sustainable are the share gains amid rebate pressures, and any updates on combo filings?

**Michael Reynolds, CFO:**  
Morning, Alex. Zepara's 14.2% NBRx share is durable via 85% payer parity and lower GI issues, with $1.2-1.4 billion FY guide; OncoVance 11.5% in ADCs benefits from StableLink tech. Rebates stable at 22% gross-to-net via optimized management. NovaKine-7/NovaTox-19 TNBC BLA rolling under Project Orbis, frontline OncoVance sNDA Q4 data—peaks $8 billion combined.

**Operator:**  
There are no further questions at this time.

**Dr. Emily Carter, CEO:**  
Thank you for your questions. In closing, I want to thank our employees for their hard work and dedication. We are confident in our ability to continue to execute on our strategic priorities and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

**Sarah Johnson, Vice President of Investor Relations:**  
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the NovaBio Therapeutics Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. Have a great day.

**Operator:**  
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
